subject: Clarify DPA notification windows, liaison & evidence transfer (FinVault)
body:
From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@finvault.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: FinVault Legal <legal@finvault.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify DPA notification windows, liaison & evidence transfer

Hi Lauren / Kimberly,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we prepare to finalize the DPA appendix, two items remain blockers for our legal and security teams: (1) the incident notification timeline language (we're trying to reconcile a 48h operational notice vs. a 72h contractual window), and (2) the practical process for transferring forensic artifacts across borders when evidence must be preserved for downstream investigations.

Specifically, can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood will commit to an initial operational notice to customers within 48 hours of detection and a contractual written notification within 72 hours, or if the contractual text needs to be the same for both?
- Who will be the named liaison for cross-border forensic handovers (we need an org/role rather than an individual name) and the process to request a snapshot/export?
- How will Redwood treat telemetry and raw logs that may contain EU personal data when providing evidence to an external vendor — will you provide sanitized exports, an escrowed forensic snapshot, or direct pass-through under a Data Transfer Agreement?

We'd like to avoid protracted redlines. Attaching our current suggested wording for Section 7 and a matrix of the types of evidence we typically request.

Attachments: forensic_scope_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), finvault-suggested-section7.docx

Thanks,
Alice Wong
Head of Security Operations, FinVault
alice.wong@finvault.com

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@finvault.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA notification windows, liaison & evidence transfer

Alice — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Below are Redwood's proposed positions to unblock the DPA redlines. I'll loop in Legal if you want final wording pushed into the doc.

1) Notification windows: Redwood proposes an operational alert to customers within 48 hours of detection (operational meaning an initial incident classification/summary) and a contractual written notice "without undue delay and no later than 72 hours from confirmation of the incident affecting customer data." We think this preserves our SOC/ops cadence while giving customers a guaranteed contractual backstop.

2) Liaison & request process: We will name a role-based liaison: "Privacy & Forensics Liaison (PrivacyOps)" — requests are made via a secure ticket through our shared control plane and include a short form (incident ID, evidence type, jurisdiction). We will commit to acknowledging requests within 8 hours and providing a plan for evidence handover within 48 hours of acknowledgement.

3) Evidence exports / cross-border: For telemetry/raw logs that may contain EU personal data, we offer two options: (A) an encrypted forensic snapshot stored in an escrow-like bucket, accessible to authorized vendors under a Data Transfer Addendum (with KMS-wrapped keys and audit logs), or (B) a sanitized export where we redact obvious PII fields prior to handover. We are open to option A for regulated customers who require full forensics; it will require DTA/contract amendments to define access controls and egress.

If FinVault is comfortable with 48h ops / 72h contractual and the escrow snapshot pathway, we can draft the precise Section 7 language and an SLA appendix for evidence handover.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsellor, Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-dpa-section7-draft.docx)

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2027 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA notification windows, liaison & evidence transfer

Quick internal note: leaning toward Option A (escrow snapshot) for this account given FinVault's regulated profile. Two commercial considerations:
- We should include an SLA credit carve-out clause if the handover requires extraordinary engineering time (>8 hours of SE/CD time) or incurs egress bandwidth costs.
- Confirm whether the escrow snapshot is considered a "subprocessor transfer" event vs. evidence access; we need to ensure our wording doesn't accidentally trigger subprocessor notification obligations in other DPAs.

If legal is comfortable, I'll propose a limited exception in the SOW or an addendum for forensic handovers that pre-authorizes certain vendors (i.e., Dan Myers at Osiris).

Ben
Director, Customer Security (on-call)

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA notification windows, liaison & evidence transfer

Ben — agree on the addendum approach. Operational notes: if we provide an escrow snapshot, engineering will require a ticket with data retention window, export scope, and vendor credentials. That should be referenced in the DPA appendix (so it's not ad-hoc). Also proposing we require a signed non-disclosure + a forensic access request form before any export.

I'll draft a one-paragraph exception for the SOW and circulate.

Marissa
Head of Customer Security Programs

---

From: Dan Myers <dan.myers@osiris-forensics.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@finvault.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: FinVault Legal <legal@finvault.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA notification windows, liaison & evidence transfer

Thanks for the ping — Dan from Osiris. From a vendor perspective, Option A (encrypted escrow snapshot) is preferable for full-chain forensics. Two practical asks: (1) a documented export manifest so we know exactly which tables/indices are included; and (2) confirmation of key-wrapping and access-review cadence (we prefer a 7-day access window per request).

We're happy to sign Redwood's forensic access form and the standard DTA.

Regards,
Dan Myers
Principal Forensic Engineer, Osiris Forensics
dan.myers@osiris-forensics.com
(attachment: osiris-ops-checklist.pdf)

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alice Wong <alice.wong@finvault.com>, FinVault Legal <legal@finvault.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA notification windows, liaison & evidence transfer

Team — thanks for the quick responses. Action items and agreed positions below so we can finalize the DPA appendix this week:

1) Notification timing: Redwood will commit to an initial operational alert within 48 hours of detection and a contractual written notice within 72 hours of confirmed impact to customer data. We'll add the phrase "subject to reasonable investigation time to confirm affected scope" to avoid false-positives creating contractual triggers.

2) Liaison: Redwood will reference the role "Privacy & Forensics Liaison (PrivacyOps)" in Section 7. The request flow will be via a secure ticket with an acknowledgement SLA (8 hours) and handover plan (within 48 hours).

3) Evidence transfer: We'll proceed with Option A (encrypted escrow snapshot) for FinVault; Osiris to be pre-authorized in an addendum and will receive a 7-day key-wrapped access window per request. Engineering requires an export manifest and the signed forensic access form.

4) Commercial carve-outs: Marissa/Ben to draft an addendum language limiting extraordinary SE time and bandwidth egress to pre-negotiated hourly rates or credits.

5) Legal: I'll push the suggested Section 7 into the redlined DPA and share a DocuSign link for the addendum.

I'll upload the redlined doc and the export matrix to the HubSpot deal record (link below). Please flag any outstanding items before EOD Wednesday.

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FIN-4721

Thanks,
Lauren

(Attachments referenced in thread: forensic_scope_matrix.xlsx; redwood-dpa-section7-draft.docx; osiris-ops-checklist.pdf)
